lorenz.title: Lorenz curves at iteration 1,499
lorenz.caption: For each of the 30 worlds (thin blue lines), after its last game: the poorest share x of its agents holds the share y of all tokens. The yellow line is the median over the worlds at each x; the dashed diagonal is a world where everyone holds the same. The further a curve sags below the diagonal, the more unequal the world ([How worlds are measured](how-worlds-are-measured.md), and the diagram there).
lorenz.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's frames, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/frames/`, read with `gol_store.read_frame(run, index)`; frame `2·t` is iteration *t* after reproduction and frame `2·t + 1` after the game.

1. Read each run's last frame (iteration 1,499, `phase` 2) and its `tokens`.
2. Sort the tokens from smallest to largest; the curve passes through the points (i / n, (t₁ + … + tᵢ) / T) for i = 0 … n.
3. Interpolate each curve at x = 0, 0.01, …, 1 and take the median there.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py tokens`.

distribution.title: How many tokens agents hold
distribution.caption: Of all agents alive after the last game of the 30 worlds, the share that hold at least x tokens, for every x. Both axes are logarithmic: a straight falling line here would be a power law.
distribution.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's frames, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/frames/`, read with `gol_store.read_frame(run, index)`; frame `2·t` is iteration *t* after reproduction and frame `2·t + 1` after the game.

1. Pool the `tokens` of the last frame of every run.
2. For every value x that occurs, the share of agents with at least x.

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py tokens`.

gini.title: Inequality of wealth (Gini)
gini.caption: After every game. The line is the median of the worlds at each iteration, the darker band holds the middle half of them (from the 25th to the 75th percentile) and the paler band nine in ten (5th to 95th).
gini.recipe:
**Runs.** The 30 baseline runs `B1-100000-s001` … `B1-100000-s030`: the baseline B1 at 100,000 tokens, seeds 1 to 30, 1,500 iterations each (every setting is listed in [Thirty worlds](a-worlds-life.md#thirty-worlds)). They are made with `python3 gol_lab.py run E10`.

**Data.** From each run's `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/stats.jsonl`, which holds one row per recorded phase: `phase` 1 is the world just after reproduction, `phase` 2 just after the game, and every statistic is a field of the row (see [What a run records](frames-and-stats.md)).

1. Take every run's rows with `phase` = 2 and the statistic `gini` ([What a run records](frames-and-stats.md)).
2. Cut the 1,500 iterations into 600 stretches of 2.5 and take each world's mean in each stretch.
3. In each stretch, take the median, the 25th and 75th and the 5th and 95th percentiles of those means over the worlds that still have a value there (a world that died has none after its death).

**To make it again:** `python3 book_figures.py tokens`.

tokens-degree.title: Tokens against connections, world of seed 1 at the end
tokens-degree.caption: Each dot is one of the 14,870 agents alive after the last game of the world with seed 1: how many connections it has (spread sideways a little so that agents with the same number do not hide each other) and how many tokens it holds.
tokens-degree.recipe:
**Runs.** `B1-100000-s001`.

**Data.** From each run's frames, `GraphOfLifeRuns/<run>/frames/`, read with `gol_store.read_frame(run, index)`; frame `2·t` is iteration *t* after reproduction and frame `2·t + 1` after the game.
